footer.blurb: Narvyaka preserves first-hand human experience in the person's own voice, so the next generation does not have to start from nothing.

hero.tagline: Because No Generation Should Start From Zero.
hero.intro: A lifetime of learning should not disappear in a moment. Narvyaka records what a person actually learned — in their own voice, in their own words — and keeps it where the next person can find it.

problem.heading: The knowledge is real. The record is not.
paragraphs: Every day, people leave this world carrying knowledge that exists nowhere else. Not published, not filmed, not written down — carried. A method that took thirty years to get right. A mistake that cost everything and was never repeated. The reason a decision was made the way it was.
It is not lost because it was unimportant. It is lost because nobody was there with a recorder, and because the person carrying it did not think of it as knowledge. They thought of it as their life.
So the next person starts again. Same mistake, same cost, same thirty years. Not because the answer did not exist — because it was never written down in a place they could reach.

items.title: Preserve your experience
items.body: Record one thing you know that another person should not have to discover again from nothing. Twenty minutes, in your own voice.

items.title: Record someone you know
items.body: A parent, a grandparent, a retired colleague, a neighbour. You ask the questions. We give you the questions to ask.

items.title: Become a founding volunteer
items.body: Interviewers, writers, translators, researchers, photographers, technologists. The archive is built by people, not software.

howItWorks.heading: One record, four parts
howItWorks.intro: Every Wisdom Record is made of the same four things. Nothing is interpreted, summarised or rewritten by a machine.

items.title: Voice
items.body: The person's own recording. This is the record. Everything else supports it.

items.title: Written note
items.body: A readable version of what was said, so it can be searched, translated and read.

items.title: Photographs
items.body: A face, a place, a tool, a handwritten page. Optional, and always the contributor's choice.

items.title: Identity
items.body: Who said it, where, and in what context — or 'Anonymous Contributor', if that is what they choose.

preserve.heading: A Lifetime of Learning Should Not Disappear in a Moment.
preserve.intro: You are about to make one Wisdom Record. It has four parts: your voice, a written note, photographs if you want them, and your identity — on whatever terms you choose. Nothing you write here is published automatically. Everything is reviewed by a person, and you can change or withdraw it at any point before that.
preserve.testIntro: There is no bar to clear and no form to pass. These five questions are simply how we think about it — if a record does any one of them, it belongs in the archive.

test.title: Does it save someone time?
test.body: Something that took you years to work out, that another person could have in an hour.

test.title: Does it help avoid a mistake?
test.body: A wrong turn you took, described clearly enough that someone else can see it coming.

test.title: Does it reduce suffering?
test.body: Knowledge that would have made a hard thing less hard, had someone known it in time.

test.title: Does it preserve something that might disappear?
test.body: A craft, a method, a language of work, a way of doing something that fewer people now know.

test.title: Does it inspire someone to live or work better?
test.body: Not motivation. Evidence — that a life or a way of working was possible.

preserve.timeNote: Most records take twenty to forty minutes. Your answers save in this browser as you go, so a lost connection does not cost you your work.

afterSubmit.heading: Thank you. Your record has been received.
afterSubmit.body: It is now with a person, not a system. Nothing is published until a human being has read it and confirmed it is exactly as you meant it. If you gave us a way to reach you, we will write to you before anything goes live.

recordSomeone.heading: Begin With Someone You Know.
recordSomeone.intro: The most valuable records in this archive will not be made by people who came looking for us. They will be made by someone who sat down with a person they already knew, and asked.
who: An aunt, uncle or elder in the family
A retired colleague, teacher or mentor
A neighbour who has done one thing for forty years
Someone whose craft or trade is no longer widely practised
Anyone who has said, more than once, "nobody does it that way any more"

how.title: Ask first, record second.
how.body: Consent comes before the recorder is switched on, and it is theirs to withdraw at any time.

how.title: Let them finish.
how.body: The most useful part of an answer usually comes after the pause you were about to fill.

how.title: Ask for the specific.
how.body: Not "what did you learn" but "what happened, and what did you do". Detail is what makes a record usable.

how.title: Do not correct them.
how.body: Their account is the record. Where something is uncertain, it is marked as their account — not removed.

recordSomeone.consentBody: You are filling this in on someone else's behalf, so we need to know they agreed to it. Their record stays theirs: they can review it, change it, restrict it or withdraw it at any time.

volunteer.heading: Become a Founding Volunteer.
volunteer.intro: Narvyaka is built by people. At this stage there is no staff, no funding round and no product team — there is a method, and there are people willing to sit with someone and ask good questions carefully. If that is you, this is the useful thing you can do.

roles.title: Interviewer
roles.body: Sits with a contributor, asks the questions in Part V, and does not rush them.

roles.title: Writer
roles.body: Turns a recording into a readable Wisdom Note without changing what was meant.

roles.title: Translator
roles.body: Carries a record into another language, and marks what does not translate cleanly.

roles.title: Researcher
roles.body: Checks what can be checked, and is honest about what cannot.

roles.title: Photographer
roles.body: Makes one good photograph of a person, a place, or the thing they made.

roles.title: Technologist
roles.body: Keeps the archive readable in fifty years, which is mostly a question of formats and discipline.

roles.title: Archivist
roles.body: Classifies, files and keeps the record consistent as the collection grows.

roles.title: Community organiser
roles.body: Finds the people whose knowledge would otherwise never reach us.

expectations: One record done carefully is worth more than ten done quickly.
Consent is not a checkbox. If someone hesitates, you stop.
You will encounter things you are not sure how to handle. Say so rather than deciding alone.
Nothing you collect is yours to publish. Every record goes through review.
volunteer.formIntro: Founding volunteers are reviewed personally. There is no automated stage and no scoring.

afterSubmit.heading: Thank you — your application is in.
afterSubmit.body: A person will read this, not a filter. Because this is the founding stage, replies take time, and everyone who applies gets one.

about.heading: A human being's knowledge, made known.

stage1.mission: To preserve first-hand human experience — the methods, mistakes, decisions and skills that people actually carry — and to keep it accessible to whoever needs it next.
stage1.vision: A world where a person beginning something difficult can find out what the last person learned, instead of starting from nothing.
stage1.belief: Knowledge that only exists inside one person is one accident away from being gone. Most of what human beings know has never been written down — and most of what has been written down was written by the few people who had the means to write.
stage1.name: Nar + Vyakta. A human being's knowledge, made known.
stage1.nameBody: Nar is a person. Vyakta is that which has been expressed — brought out of the unexpressed and into a form another person can receive. Narvyaka is the act of doing that with a life's worth of learning.

stage2.label: The deeper meaning
stage2.heading: Three who carried what they were told.
stage2.intro: The name has a second reading. It is not necessary in order to use Narvyaka, and it is placed here rather than at the front for exactly that reason.

figures.name: Narada
figures.body: The one who moved between worlds carrying what he had heard, and whose function was transmission itself — the messenger who kept knowledge in motion between those who held it and those who needed it.

figures.name: Vyasa
figures.body: The compiler. The one who took what was scattered and oral and at risk of dispersal, and arranged it so that it could survive being handed on.

figures.name: Kakabhushundi
figures.body: The one who lived across ages and remembered — the witness whose value was not what he did, but what he retained and could still recount long after everyone else had gone.

stage2.closing: Transmission, compilation, memory. Preserve. Connect. Continue.

howItWorks.heading: What a Wisdom Record is.
howItWorks.intro: A Wisdom Record is one piece of first-hand experience, captured in a form that can outlast the person who gave it. It is deliberately small. One record is one thing you know — not your life story.

parts.title: 1. The voice
parts.body: The contributor's own recording, kept exactly as it was made. This is the primary record. It is not cleaned up, re-read by someone else, or replaced by a summary. Hearing how someone says a thing is part of what they said.

parts.title: 2. The written note
parts.body: A readable version of the recording, so that it can be searched, quoted and translated. Transcription and translation only. Nothing is interpreted, expanded, dramatised or rewritten — if the note says it, the contributor said it.

parts.title: 3. The photographs
parts.body: Up to five images: the person, the place, the tool, the handwritten page. Entirely optional. A record with no photographs is a complete record.

parts.title: 4. The identity
parts.body: Who gave this, where they were, what they did. Identity can be full, partial, or withheld entirely — a record can be published as 'Anonymous Contributor' without losing any of its value.

audioBody: Audio first is a deliberate choice, not a limitation of the budget. Video needs a room, a light, a camera and a person willing to be looked at. Audio needs a phone and somebody willing to talk.

The difference matters because of who we are trying to reach. The people whose knowledge is most at risk of disappearing are rarely the people most comfortable in front of a camera. Asking for video would quietly filter the archive down to the confident — and the confident are already recorded.
Audio is also smaller, cheaper to keep for decades, and easier to transcribe and translate. Video can come later, for the records that want it. Wisdom cannot wait for the production.
howItWorks.storageIntro: Every record is stored in three forms at once, because the thing that destroys archives is not fire — it is formats nobody can open any more.

storage.title: The original evidence
storage.body: The untouched audio file and the original photographs, exactly as they came from the contributor. Nothing is ever edited in place. If we are wrong about everything else, this survives.

storage.title: The human-readable form
storage.body: Plain text and standard images that a person can open in fifty years with no special software — the version that survives us, our website, and whatever technology replaces it.

storage.title: The machine-readable form
storage.body: Structured data, so a record can be found by someone who does not yet know it exists. This is what makes an archive usable rather than merely full.

howItWorks.reviewBody: Every submission arrives with the status 'pending review'. A person reads it, checks it with the contributor where anything is unclear, and only then is it published — at whatever access level the contributor chose. There is no automatic pipeline from a form to a public page, and there will not be one.
howItWorks.verificationIntro: Records are not silently presented as fact. Each carries one of exactly three labels, and no record is left unmarked.

verification.body: Supported by records, artefacts or independent sources that can be pointed to.
First-hand testimony from the person who was there. Not independently confirmed, and not treated as lesser for it.
Knowledge passed down and reported as it was received, with the chain of telling shown rather than hidden.

howItWorks.sampleIntro: This is the shape of a finished record. Until a real one exists, this is an illustration.

browse.heading: What has been preserved so far.
browse.emptyBody: There is nothing published here yet — not because it is broken, but because it is new. The first records are being made now. Every one that appears here will have been given deliberately by a person, and read by a person before it went up.

founder.heading: Why this exists.
founder.placeholderNotice: This page is a placeholder. Replace the text below with Appendix B of the Master Reference, verbatim — either in src/data/site.json under `founder.letter`, or directly in the Studio.
letter: My great-grandfather and grandfather passed away before I was old enough to ask the right questions.

I know what they did. I do not know how they did it, what it cost them, what they tried first, or what they would have told me not to bother with. That knowledge existed. It was in the room with me. And it left without anyone thinking to write it down, because nobody involved — including them — thought of it as knowledge worth recording. It was just their life.

I have since found that almost everybody has this same gap, and almost everybody discovers it about ten years too late. The questions arrive when you are old enough to need the answers, which is usually after the person who had them has gone.

Narvyaka is the attempt to close that gap by a few years, for a few people, deliberately. Not to build a database of everything. To make sure that when someone does think to ask, there is somewhere for the answer to go.
If you have someone to ask, please ask them now. Whether you use this or not.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.placeholderNotice: Placeholder — pending legal review (Master Reference Part XV). The commitments below describe how the system is actually built today, and are what the reviewed policy must not contradict.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: Only what you type into a form or record into a microphone, plus the technical minimum needed to serve the page. There is no analytics script, no advertising pixel, no third-party tracker and no cookie used to follow you between sites.

sections.title: What we do with a recording
sections.body: We transcribe it and, where relevant, translate it. That is the whole list. Recordings are not used to train AI models, and will not be, unless a contributor gives separate, explicit, specific consent for that purpose — which we do not currently ask for.

sections.title: Who can see your record
sections.body: Whoever you chose, at the access level you set when you submitted it. The default is that nothing is public. A record can be public, public but anonymous, family-only, restricted to research use, private, preserved but unpublished, published after a date you name, or released only after your death.

sections.title: Changing your mind
sections.body: You can review, correct, restrict or withdraw your record at any time, before or after publication. Withdrawal means removal from the public archive; tell us if you also want the underlying files destroyed, and they will be.

sections.title: Where it is stored
sections.body: On infrastructure operated by Cloudflare. Recordings and images are held in object storage, the structured record in a database, both under our account and neither shared with, sold to, or licensed to anyone.

sections.title: Children and minors
sections.body: This is not a service for children. Contributions are intended for people aged 30 or over; a younger contributor may apply, but their submission is reviewed by a person before anything is accepted.

sections.title: How to reach us
sections.body: Until a permanent address is published, use the contact route given on the volunteer page. A named contact will be added here before any record is made public.

terms.heading: Terms of Use
terms.placeholderNotice: Placeholder — pending legal review (Master Reference Part XV).

sections.title: What Narvyaka is
sections.body: An archive of first-hand accounts, given voluntarily. It is not a professional, medical, legal, financial or safety advice service, and nothing in it should be relied on as one.

sections.title: Accounts are accounts
sections.body: Records are what a person said happened. Each carries a label — Documented, Contributor's Account, or Family Tradition — describing how much independent support it has. Read the label before you rely on the record.

sections.title: Who owns a record
sections.body: The contributor. By submitting, you grant Narvyaka permission to preserve your record and to make it available at the access level you selected, and nothing beyond that. You may withdraw that permission.

sections.title: Using what you find here
sections.body: Read it, learn from it, quote it with attribution. Do not republish records wholesale, scrape the archive, or use it to build a commercial dataset. Records are not licensed for AI training.

sections.title: What we will remove
sections.body: Anything submitted without the subject's consent, anything that identifies a living person who did not agree to be identified, and anything a contributor asks us to remove.

sections.title: Nothing is guaranteed forever
sections.body: We intend this archive to outlast us and we build accordingly. We cannot promise permanence, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise.

consent.heading: Before you begin
consent.intro: Three things, in plain language, before you give us anything.

points.title: Your recording is transcribed and translated. Nothing else.
points.body: We write down what you said so it can be read and searched, and we translate it where that is useful. Your recording is not used to train AI systems, and will not be, unless you are separately asked and separately agree. Nothing is rewritten, summarised or interpreted on your behalf.

points.title: Nothing is published automatically.
points.body: Your record arrives marked 'pending review'. A person reads it. If anything is unclear we come back to you. Only then does it go anywhere — at the access level you choose at the end.

points.title: You stay in control of it.
points.body: You can review, edit, restrict or withdraw your record at any time, including after it is published.

consent.checkReview: I understand I can review and edit everything before it is published.
consent.checkAge: I am 30 years of age or older.
consent.ageWhy: Why 30? Because the records that help most tend to come from experience that has had time to be tested. It is a guideline, not a wall.
consent.exceptionHeading: Tell us why this shouldn't wait
consent.exceptionBody: If you are under 30 and you have something that should be recorded now, say so here. This does not block your submission — it routes it to a person to read.
consent.exceptionPlaceholder: What is it, and why does it need recording now?
consent.consentRequiredError: Please confirm the first statement before continuing.

about.heading: About you
about.intro: This is the identity part of the record. All of it can be withheld, and a withheld identity does not make a record worth less.
about.name: Your name
about.namePlaceholder: As you would like it written
about.anonymous: Keep my name private — publish this as 'Anonymous Contributor'
about.preferredName: Preferred name, or your name in its original script

about.professionPlaceholder: e.g. Weaver, civil engineer, farmer, nurse, teacher

about.contactBody: Only used to come back to you with questions and to confirm before publishing. Never published, never shared, never added to a mailing list.
about.contactPlaceholder: Optional, but it is how we confirm before publishing

record.heading: The Wisdom Record
record.intro: One question at a time. There are eight, most are short, and any of them can be skipped except the first.

questions.label: What is one experience, lesson, method, mistake, decision, skill, or memory that another person should not have to discover again from nothing?
questions.hint: Take your time with this one. Everything after it is just detail.
questions.placeholder: Say it however it comes out. It does not need to be tidy.

questions.label: What happened? When and where? Who was involved?
questions.hint: Specifics are what make a record usable years from now.
questions.placeholder: The situation, as plainly as you can tell it.

questions.label: What did you do, and why that choice?
questions.hint: Including the reasoning that seemed obvious at the time.

questions.label: What worked, what failed, and what surprised you?
questions.hint: The surprise is often the most valuable part.

questions.label: What should another person remember?
questions.hint: One or two sentences. This is what gets shown on your record's card, so it is worth saying carefully.
questions.placeholder: The one thing you would want them to carry away.

questions.label: In what situations might this not apply?
questions.hint: Knowing the limits of advice is part of the advice.

questions.label: Who else could confirm this, if anyone?
questions.hint: A person, a document, a photograph, a place. This sets how the record is labelled — and 'nobody' is a perfectly good answer.

lineage.heading: Family & learning note
lineage.question: What did the generations before you do or learn, that shaped what you know?
lineage.hint: Parents, grandparents — as much or as little as you know.
lineage.placeholder: Whatever you know, in whatever order it comes.
lineage.disclaimer: We don't ask you to research this. Only what you already know, exactly as you know it — even if it's incomplete or uncertain.

photos.heading: Photographs
photos.intro: Up to five. A face, a place, a tool, a handwritten page. A record with no photographs is a complete record — this step can be skipped entirely.
photos.dropLabel: Drag photographs here, or choose files
photos.dropHint: JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC. Up to 10 MB each.
photos.captionPlaceholder: One line, if you want one
photos.maxReached: That is five photographs — the maximum for one record.
photos.tooLarge: That file is over 10 MB. Try a smaller version.
photos.wrongType: That file type isn't supported. Use JPEG, PNG or WebP.

review.heading: Access & review
review.accessHeading: Who should be able to see this?
review.accessIntro: You can change this later. If you are unsure, choose the most private option — nothing is harder to undo than publication.

levels.title: Public
levels.body: Anyone can find and read this record, with your name on it.

levels.title: Public, anonymous
levels.body: Anyone can read it. Your name is replaced with 'Anonymous Contributor'.

levels.title: Family only
levels.body: Kept for the people you name. Not listed publicly.

levels.title: Restricted — research use
levels.body: Available to researchers on request and on record. Not published openly.

levels.title: Private
levels.body: Held for you alone. Nobody else is given access.

levels.title: Preserved, not published
levels.body: Kept safely in the archive with no publication planned. Preservation is the point.

levels.title: Publish after a date
levels.body: Held until a date you name, then published as public.

levels.title: Release after my death
levels.body: Held until we are notified and have confirmed it. Then published as public.

review.previewIntro: Read it once. Anything here can still be changed — use the step numbers at the top to go back.
review.finalNote: Submitting sends this for human review. It does not publish anything.

studio.title: Narvyaka Studio
studio.intro: Edit the site by hand — text, colours, fonts, the logo and the photographs. Changes preview instantly and are stored in this browser only. When you are happy, export them and apply them to the code.
